title: Networking, identity and security
summary: Connecting to Azure, and deciding who gets in and how they are protected.

expressroute.clue: A private connection from your network to Azure that doesn't cross the public internet

vpn-gateway.clue: Sends encrypted traffic between your network and Azure over the public internet

dns.clue: Hosts the name records of your domains on Azure's infrastructure

peering.clue: Connects two virtual networks so traffic between them stays on Microsoft's backbone

private-endpoint.clue: Gives a service a private IP address inside your virtual network

entra-id.clue: Microsoft's cloud identity service: users, groups and sign-in

sso.clue: One sign-in gives access to many applications

mfa.clue: Sign-in asks for a second proof, such as a code on your phone

passwordless.clue: Signing in with Windows Hello, an authenticator app or a security key, with no password

conditional-access.clue: Allows, blocks or challenges a sign-in based on signals such as location or device

rbac.clue: Gives a user or group a role, such as Reader, at a scope such as a resource group

zero-trust.clue: Assume breach, and verify every request explicitly, whatever network it comes from

defense-in-depth.clue: Layers of protection, so that no single failure exposes the data

defender.clue: Assesses security posture and protects workloads in Azure, on-premises and other clouds
